title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: From March 2022, a network of ILO certified youth Business Development Service Providers delivered new forms of financial and non-financial Business Development Services (BDS) to the beneficiary micro and small enterprises. Following the certification and formalization of the SIYB Association in Kigoma, quality services are provided to the target women and youth enterprises in Kasulu, Kibondo and Kakonko Districts. The BDS providers, in collaboration with the Local Government Authorities (LGAs) continued to provide business services to the target youth and women groups in terms of support to business registration and access to financial services. In this reporting period, 3 of the 15 supported youth and women enterprises received funding in form of loans from the LGA women and youth credit facility to further expand their enterprises. Some of the factors that contributed to the enterprises accessing loans, include but are not limited to; clarity of project ideas, quality of the business plans, good repayment of business loans especially for women and overall mentorship support from youth BDS providers and LGA officials trained in the auspices of One UN fund implemented by the ILO. With the support from One Fund, the ILO capacitated and certified in 2022, four local BDS providers network to support youth and women entrepreneurs though SYB modules and new BDS services including registration of business groups to the local government as a minimum qualification to acquire business credits provided under the Government’s Women and Youth Development Credit Facility and linkages to markets. The approach has contributed to ensuring the sustainability of the ILO interventions under the project, by enabling continued mentoring and integration of interventions to support youth and women entrepreneurs into district development plans. The intervention also targets LGA officials which added to the sustainability of project interventions in terms of subsequent application of the acquired knowledge. ILO continued to provide supportive supervision and monitoring of service provision to ensure that quality services are provided in line with the ILO business training tools.
